source_lines.31: Let $k$ be any field, $n\geq 1$, and $\hbar\in k$. Let $\mathfrak h_n(k)$ and $W_n(k;\hbar)$ be as in [[def-heisenberg-lie-algebra]] and [[def-polynomial-weyl-algebra]]. Since $Z$ is central, define the quotient $Q_\hbar:=U(\mathfrak h_n(k))/(Z-\hbar1)$.
source_lines.37: identifies the polynomial Weyl algebra with the central quotient
source_lines.45: form a $k$-basis of $W_n(k;\hbar)$ for every characteristic. Equivalently, in the presentation of [[def-polynomial-weyl-algebra]], the relations rewrite to these unique normal forms. If $\hbar\ne0$, scaling $p_i\mapsto\hbar p_i$ gives $W_n(k;\hbar)\cong A_n(k)$; if $\hbar=0$, the defining generators commute.
source_lines.93: The square records the maps used in steps 1.2, 3.1, and 4.1. The left vertical map sends $X_i\mapsto x_i$, $P_i\mapsto p_i$, and $Z\mapsto\hbar1$; the top and bottom maps are the quotient maps from the tensor-algebra presentations; the right vertical map is the isomorphism proved above. The proof is the algebraic argument in the numbered steps, not the picture.
